chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id together, from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani, from Hariz ibn Abd Allah al-Sijistani, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I asked him, meaning Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him),

about what Allah, Exalted and Glorious, has obligated regarding prayer, so he said: Five prayers during the night and day. I said: Did Allah, Blessed and Exalted, name them and clarify them in His Book? He said: Yes,
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to His Prophet, peace be upon him and his Family: 'Establish the prayer at the setting of the sun until the darkness of the night.'

And its setting is its vanishing, so between the setting of the sun until the darkness of the night are four prayers which He named, clarified, and set a time for, and the darkness of the night is its midpoint,
Then He said: 'And the Qur'an of the dawn. Indeed, the Qur'an of the dawn is ever witnessed.'

This is the fifth. And He, Blessed and Exalted, said regarding that: 'Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day', and its two ends are the Maghrib (sunset) and al-Ghada (early morning) prayers. 'And at the approach of the night', and that is the 'Isha al-Akhira (last evening) prayer.
And He, Exalted and Glorious, said: 'Maintain the prayers, and (in particular) the middle prayer.'

And it is the Dhuhr (noon) prayer, and it was the first prayer the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, prayed, and it is in the middle of two prayers during the day, the al-Ghada (early morning) and al-Asr (afternoon) prayers. 'And stand before Allah, devoutly obedient' during the middle prayer.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ الْوُسْطَى: The middle prayer (identified here as Dhuhr)
key_terms.طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ: The two ends of the day (morning and evening)

ai.seo_question: What are the five daily prayers and how are they derived from the Quran according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* provides a foundational Shia exegesis of the five daily prayers by explicitly linking them to Quranic verses, thereby establishing their divine origin rather than mere prophetic tradition. It offers a specific interpretation of the debated 'middle prayer' (Salat al-Wusta) as Dhuhr, noting its historical precedence as the first prayer established by the Prophet, while also defining the temporal boundaries for the night prayers. This narration is significant for resolving jurisprudential discussions regarding the timing and number of obligatory prayers through direct scriptural evidence.
